title: Two Spoons, Then This
title_candidates: The Last Rung: Neumann Finally Gets His Hands on the Trophy
Estoril, Both Ends: A Course Record, A Course Worst, And A Champion Already Home
theme: A career of Wooden Spoons and near-misses is settled in the least dramatic manner available: Stuart Neumann led the Trophy after every single round, and the only question left by Penha Longa was how many of his rivals could be persuaded to blow up behind him.
opening_hook: Open at Estoril's 8th in R4 — the hardest hole on the card (SI 1) — where the eventual champion made a 9 and it cost him precisely nothing, because the tournament had been decided two courses earlier; then rewind to a man whose CV read two Wooden Spoons and no trophies at all.

trophy_storyline.subject: Stuart Neumann's first Trophy — 156 points, 13 clear, and never headed after the opening afternoon
trophy_storyline.why_it_matters: Neumann arrived with no Trophy wins and two prior Wooden Spoons to his name, and finishes in the last four TEGs he played of 6th, 5th, 3rd and 2nd — there was exactly one rung left, and he climbed it without ever once trailing.
trophy_storyline.shape: Setup: 39 points at Oitavos Dunes opened a 5-point lead on the first day, and after two routine early exchanges on R1's 4th and 5th holes nobody drew level with him again all tournament (b08, b28, b43). Turn: 35 at Troia stretched it to 7, then 39 at Penha Longa — while the rest of the field was busy dismantling itself on the back nine — blew the margin out to 12, and the competition effectively closed there. Resolution: a 43-point R4 at Estoril, his best round of the four and a new personal best there of 92 gross (prior best 106, TEG 15), containing a quintuple-bogey 9 at the 8th, SI 1, which he could afford to treat as a rounding error (b46, b01).

jacket_storyline.subject: Gregg Williams's second Green Jacket, +66, by 16 shots
jacket_storyline.why_it_matters: The defending Trophy champion lost his title and answered by leading the gross competition after every round and posting the 5th-best Jacket total in TEG history — while the man with 9 prior Jacket wins finished 16 adrift.
jacket_storyline.shape: Setup: 89 gross at Oitavos Dunes, a personal best there (prior best 91, TEG 15), gave him a 3-shot lead, and Troia was the only genuine pressure of the tournament — Jon Baker drew level on the 11th and again on the 14th while Williams bled six shots in three holes, 13-15, and went four holes without a net par, 8-11 (b41, b48, b50). Turn: Penha Longa, where a triple at the 7th was answered by a birdie at the 5th's predecessor problem and then five holes without dropping a gross shot, 11-15, plus nine points across 13-15 — 87 gross, and the lead ballooned from 4 to 14 (b18, b23, b25, b35, b45). Resolution: 80 gross at Estoril in R4, his own Estoril personal best (prior best 86, TEG 15), with a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 14th and a double at the 9th to end a run of three straight pars, neither of which mattered by then (b03, b06, b02).

spoon_storyline.subject: Alex Baker's third Wooden Spoon, back-to-back, 127 points — and two all-time course-worst records to go with it
spoon_storyline.why_it_matters: The reigning Spoon holder from TEG 15 was bottom of the Trophy standings after every one of the four rounds and set the worst gross score TEG has ever recorded at two separate courses in the same tournament.
spoon_storyline.shape: Setup: a 9 at the 1st at Oitavos Dunes, a 9 at the 11th, and a sextuple-bogey 10 at the 17th on the way to 113 gross — a new Oitavos course-worst across 12 prior TEG visits, and 10 shots worse than his last visit (cr03, b49, b47, b37). Turn: he dropped outright to the bottom of the Spoon race on Troia's 13th and stayed there for the rest of the tournament, bleeding 13 shots over 13-17, then bled 12 more across Penha Longa's 11-14 including a quadruple-bogey 9 at the 12th (b33, b19, b26, b44). Resolution: Estoril, R4 — a 9 at the 1st, an 8 at the 3rd, a 9 at the 6th, 14 shots gone over 5-10 and a septuple-bogey 11 at the 12th, his worst hole relative to par of the tournament, for 107 gross: a new Estoril course-worst, set on the same afternoon and the same course as David Mullin's course record (b32, b39, b38, b30, b31, b09, cr02, b24).

discovered_storylines.subject: David Mullin: from the bottom of the Spoon race in R1 to the Estoril course record in R4
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: The man with 9 prior Jacket wins spent the opening afternoon at the wrong end of the Wooden Spoon table and the closing one rewriting the Estoril record book — an 80 gross that beat a mark standing across 6 prior visits.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: R1 at Oitavos Dunes, a triple bogey at the 10th drops him outright to the bottom of the Spoon race, and although 94 gross was 10 better than his last visit there, Penha Longa was worse — 98 gross, 13 shots worse than his last visit, including a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 16th, SI 1, the hardest hole on the course (b40, b05). Turn: R4 at Estoril, 45 points against 30 in R3, a 15-point swing — birdie at the 2nd, a birdie at the 7th to stop the bleeding after three dropped holes, nine points across 11-13 and pars all the way home through 16-17 (b13, b22, b04, b07, b10, b14). Resolution: 80 gross, a new Estoril course record beating the prior 86, and a 14-shot improvement on his own previous best there — achieved on the day he was, in Trophy terms, an irrelevance, and while finishing 16 shots behind Williams for the Jacket (cr01).

discovered_storylines.subject: The Baker brothers and Penha Longa's 12th
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: On a par 5 rated SI 17 — one of the two easiest holes on the card — the two brothers in the field posted a 9 and a 10 in the same round, and both had already gone missing on the same stretch of back nine.
discovered_storylines.shape: Setup: Penha Longa's 11th-13th, where Jon Baker bled 11 shots in three holes and went three holes without a net par — a double at the 11th, a quintuple-bogey 10 at the 12th, a quadruple-bogey 8 at the 13th (b21, b27, b34, b42). Turn: his brother arrived at the same hole and returned a quadruple-bogey 9, part of 12 shots lost across 11-14 and three holes without a net par (b44, b19, b26). Resolution: the family habit travelled — Jon Baker followed up with a quadruple-bogey 8 at Estoril's 11th, SI 2, in R4, and finished 4 points clear of his brother, which is the narrowest of all the week's margins and the only one either of them will want to discuss (b36).

vehicle_fit_response.note: Alex Baker's seven blow-ups are real and they carry the Spoon story wholesale, but a catalogue frame was the last report's device and the week belongs to Neumann's first Trophy after two Spoons — the catalogue lives inside spoon_storyline instead of framing the report.

why_the_champion_won: He built it rather than inherited it: best in the field in R1, R2 and R3, three of the four rounds won outright, ahead of Williams in every round head-to-head, and a 43-point closing round at Estoril — even an average round from Williams instead of his worst would not have flipped it.
